required_work: Unify the remaining ~31 constraint-divergent shared $def names that are consistency work rather than authority work — hash, canonicalDateTime, nullableHash, ref, canonicalRef, canonicalRefs, artifactRef, commitmentRef, deploymentProfileRef, lifecycleState, materializationRef, operation, operationEntry, schemaRef, sha256Hash, refs, receiptRefs, evidenceRefs, protocolPrincipalOrRuntimeRef, publicCommitmentRef, nullableDateTime, nullableReceiptRef, goalRunProfileRevisionHashTuples, boundCoordinates, approvalAuthority, authorizedEffect, principalAuthorityBindingStatement and the tail — under the same tighter-not-looser constraint.
objective: The non-authority half of the measured shared-$def divergence: 169 unregistered duplicated names across 143 contracts, ~35 constraint-divergent, of which the eight authority-bearing names are owned by m2-authority-ref-shape-unification-successor. Nothing downstream is made unsafe by this remainder, but a name that means two things is a latent trap for the next family that copies whichever it finds first. M9_SHARED_SCHEMA_DEF_CONSISTENCY_EXIT=0.
falsifiable_claim: The claim fails if any remaining name is left constraint-divergent without a recorded reason, if unification widened any family's admissible set, or if a unified name is left unregistered under the byte-identity bar.
selected_profile: The ~31 non-authority constraint-divergent names measured at b63353a6e.
current_implementation_evidence: DIVERGENCE TAXONOMY (director-measured 2026-08-02 at b63353a6e, annotation-stripped so none of the 35 is prose-only): (1) LOOSENING — the same shape bounded in most families and unbounded in a few: receiptRef is {1,248} in 16 files but [^\\s]+ unbounded in 2 and {1,500} in 1; policyRef unbounded in 1 of 28; evidenceRef unbounded in 2; grantRef unbounded in 5 of 11. (2) NON-NESTED SCHEME SETS — the sharpest case: evidenceRef admits (evidence|receipt|artifact|attestation):// in 9 files and (evidence|assurance-evidence|artifact):// in 2. Those sets do not nest — attestation:// is valid evidence in one family and malformed in another. That is a semantic seam, not a length quibble. (3) DELIBERATE NARROWING, WHICH IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE TOUCHED — receiptRef is ^receipt://ltr_[0-9a-f]{64}$ in 2 files and asar_[0-9a-f]{64} in 1; grantRef is ^grant://wallet[.]network/approval/sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ in 4. OWNER-BOUND UNIFICATION CONSTRAINT (not negotiable by the implementing cut; mechanism is the cut's choice, this constraint is not): unification runs toward the TIGHTER shape, never the looser. A family that has narrowed KEEPS its narrowing — expressed as a registered base plus family refinement, or as a separately registered name. Collapsing the four wallet-approval grants into the shared 11-copy grantRef would widen them from an exact wallet.network approval form to any grant:// string; that is a regression, not a unification, and it is the specific failure this constraint exists to prevent. The authority-bearing subset (receiptRef, grantRef, evidenceRef, policyRef, authorityEffect, walletApprovalGrant, signatureProof, ed25519Signature) is explicitly NOT this record's — owner ruling 2026-08-02 assigns it to M2 so M5-M8 are not built on the seam.
